environment.tool: manual review of release/000004 + live compiled binary against a strict exec peer with raw line capture

findings.description: The URI is spec.substr(slash)+path.substr(loc->path.size())+q. With an exact location match the remainder is empty, so GET /api?cmd=whoami emits GET /exec?cmd=whoami HTTP/1.1 - three tokens. A strict parser reads token 1 as the exec route with the query attached and runs whoami. Bare GET /api emits GET /exec HTTP/1.1 and runs id. No percent-encoding in the client request. Requires a proxy_pass URI naming the exec route with no trailing space.
findings.title: Exact-match URI without a trailing space keeps a 3-token line, so an attacker query alone executes a chosen command on a strict parser

findings.description: A quoted trailing space in the URI makes GET /api emit GET /exec  HTTP/1.1, four tokens, two spaces. A whitespace-splitting upstream executes the default command. CL:0 POST also works and emits POST. The attacker sends only the path; the command is the upstream default. Requires the quoted space and a whitespace-splitting upstream.
findings.title: A quoted space in the proxy_pass URI is the separator, so a bare GET /api executes the upstream default command with no encoding

findings.description: The gate rejects any Content-Length other than the literal 0 with 400 and does not close, so a POST body request fails while a GET with a trailing request line and no CL is answered 400 and the leftover is parsed and proxied, producing a second execution from one write. Requires keep-alive. Control GET /hello.txt 200.
findings.title: A trailing request line with no Content-Length survives an accepted-then-400 request and is proxied as a second request

limitations: SEC-002 needs a whitespace-splitting upstream and SEC-001 a strict 3-token reader
RCE is upstream-side; no local exec
